Trivia[edit | edit source]

\n
Concept art of Ash's hat from the original series
\n
Ash's drawing of a Dewgong
\n
  • Ash was designed by Atsuko Nishida.[2]
    • \n
  • Ash's height is around 4'7" (140 cm).[3]
    • \n
  • Ash's hat in the original series was similar to Red's hat in his original design from Pokémon Red and Green before undergoing several changes until the final design.
    • \n
  • Ash originally wanted a Squirtle to be his first partner Pokémon, but Professor Oak told him it was taken by a Trainer who was not late.
    • \n
  • In the animated series, Ash is the first and, so far, only Trainer:\n
    • With a known hometown to not be native to any of the regions he is the Champion of.
      • \n
    • With access to Z-Moves, Dynamax/Gigantamax, and Mega Evolution at the same time.\n
      • Who has used more than one of those in a single battle.
      • \n
    • Shown to have won two of the same Gym Badge, as he's earned a Rain Badge from both Juan and Wallace.
    • \n
  • Ash is the only Champion in the animated series to own a Mythical Pokémon.
    • \n
  • Ash has never caught another Electric-type Pokémon other than Pikachu.
    • \n
  • Ash has never officially owned a female-only Pokémon.\n
    • While he has technically owned a Legendary Pokémon in Solgaleo, he has never officially caught one in a Poké Ball.
    • \n
  • Ash has caught at least one of the first partner Pokémon of every region he has visited, except for Galar.
    • \n
  • Ash has caught at least one Flying-type Pokémon in every series.\n
    • Moreover, Flying is the most common type among Ash's non-temporary Pokémon under his ownership, with a total of twelve representants.
    • \n
  • As of A Chilling Curse!, Ash has caught at least one Pokémon belonging to all eighteen types (this includes Pokémon he owns or has owned that have been retroactively made Fairy-type).\n
    • Also, as of Battling Turned Up to Eleven!, he has used at least one move of every type with his Pokémon.
    • \n
  • All of Ash's Grass-type Pokémon are part of a three-stage evolutionary line.
    • \n
  • Ash's favorite move is Thunderbolt, as revealed by himself in Climbing the Walls!.
    • \n
  • Ash is still considered a 10-year-old in promotional materials and in main series episodes as recent as Sleuths for Truth!, despite at least a year having been implied to have passed between A Goldenrod Opportunity and Best Wishes Until We Meet Again!.\n
    • Kunihiko Yuyama, creative supervisor for Pokémon Journeys: The Series and executive director for prior series, has stated in an interview with Daniel Arsham in Arsham's Pokédex, a collection of Pokémon-related artwork, that Ash does not age because the animated series is set in an endless early summer.
    • \n
  • When Veronica Taylor was interviewed in the documentary "Adventures in Voice Acting", she stated that during her audition for the role of Ash, he was known as Casey at the time. This name would later be given to a recurring character from Johto.
    • \n
  • Ash can draw, as shown in Up Close and Personable! when he drew a Dewgong. However, his drawing was insulted by Angie.
    • \n
  • Ash has been shown to be a good climber at various points in the animated series, such as in Enter Iris and Axew!, Climbing the Walls, and Some Kind of Laziness!, to the point of Misty saying "He climbs like a Mankey" in Celebi: The Voice of the Forest, and Brock calling him a "human Aipom" in Lucario and the Mystery of Mew.
    • \n
  • Ash has lost once to every Normal-type Gym Leader he has met. Out of the four Normal-type Gym Leaders he has battled against, Cheren is the only one against whom Ash has never won.
    • \n
  • The only region where Ash didn't lose any official Gym battles is the Orange Archipelago.\n
    • Also, Ash did not lose any official trials in Pokémon the Series: Sun & Moon, although he has lost to Nanu in an unofficial battle.
    • \n
  • Ever since facing Wattson in Watt's with Wattson?, Ash has not won a Gym Badge in the same episode in which he meets the Gym Leader.
    • \n
  • If only Trainer battles are counted, Ash's longest winning streak lasted a total of 87 episodes, spanning from his loss to Rinto in Trials of a Budding Master! to his loss to Misty in A Fated Face-Off!.\n
    • If not, as all of his eligible Pokémon were defeated in a Raid Battle against an Articuno in Battling in the Freezing Raid!, the longest period Ash has been on a winning streak is exactly 70 episodes, going from Battles in the Sky! to A Meeting of Two Journeys!.
    • \n
  • Ash has defeated more regional Champions onscreen in the animated series than any other Trainer, having won against Iris, Steven, Cynthia, and Leon.\n
    • Additionally, he has also defeated Wallace, the former Hoenn Champion.
    • \n
  • Ash shares at least one Pokémon of the same evolutionary line with one of his rivals in each series.
    • \n
  • Time After Time! and The Mew from Here! are the only main series episodes during his time as a protagonist to not feature Ash in any capacity.
    • \n
  • In promotional material for the Manalo Conference, Ash was given the title of (Japanese: ゼンリョクチャレンジャ Full-force challenger).
    • \n
  • National Ash Ketchum Day is celebrated every September 15, the anniversary of Ash's first Pokémon League Conference victory, first being celebrated on said victory's first-year anniversary in 2020.
    • \n
  • In the Pokémon: Twilight Wings episode Letter, a Trainer who bears a resemblance to Ash can be seen at the entrance to Wyndon Stadium with a Pikachu.
    • \n
  • Although Ash has been retired from the role of main protagonist as of Pokémon Horizons: The Series, Senior Marketing Director of The Pokémon Company International, Andy Gose, has not ruled out the possibility of him reappearing at some point due to him still being around in the world of Pokémon.[4]
\n
